text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"SQLite's default maximum string or BLOB length is one billion bytes.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 0 states that SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH defines the maximum bytes in a string or BLOB and its default is 1 billion.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"The maximum number of bytes in a string or BLOB in SQLite is defined by the preprocessor macro SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH. The default value of this macro is 1 billion (1 thousand million or 1,000,000,000)."}]},{"claim_text":"A table can have up to 2000 columns by default.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 gives the default setting for SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN as 2000.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"The default setting for SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN is 2000."}]},{"claim_text":"The default maximum column limit can be raised at compile time to as many as 32767.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 states SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN can be changed at compile time to values as large as 32767.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"You can change it at compile time to values as large as 32767."}]},{"claim_text":"Expression trees may nest 1000 levels deep by default.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 2 states SQLITE_MAX_EXPR_DEPTH determines maximum expression tree depth and the current default is 1000.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"The SQLITE_MAX_EXPR_DEPTH parameter determines the maximum expression tree depth. If the value is 0, then no limit is enforced. The current implementation has a default value of 1000."}]},{"claim_text":"A compound SELECT can have up to 500 terms.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 states the maximum number of terms is SQLITE_MAX_COMPOUND_SELECT, which defaults to 500.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"The maximum number of terms is SQLITE_MAX_COMPOUND_SELECT which defaults to 500."}]},{"claim_text":"By default ten databases can be attached to one connection.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 states the number of simultaneously attached databases is limited by SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED, set to 10 by default.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"The number of simultaneously attached databases is limited to SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED which is set to 10 by default."}]},{"claim_text":"The attached-database limit can never be pushed past 125.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 4 states the maximum number of attached databases cannot be increased above 125.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"The maximum number of attached databases cannot be increased above 125."}]},{"claim_text":"With the default page size and the default maximum page count, a database can grow to roughly 17.5 TB.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 states that with the default max page count and default page size of 4096 bytes, the maximum database size is about 17.5 terabytes.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"Since version 3.45.0 (2024-01-15), 4294967294 is also the default value for SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_COUNT. When used with the default page size of 4096 bytes, this gives a maximum database size of about 17.5 terabytes."}]},{"claim_text":"A database file can grow to roughly 281 TB with 65536-byte pages.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 5 states that if page size is increased to the maximum of 65536 bytes, the database file can grow to about 281 terabytes.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"If the page size is increased to the maximum of 65536 bytes, then the database file can grow to be as large as about 281 terabytes."}]},{"claim_text":"Roughly 17.5 TB is about one sixteenth of roughly 281 TB.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage gives about 17.5 terabytes and about 281 terabytes; 281 divided by 16 is approximately 17.56, so about 17.5 is about one sixteenth of 281.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"about 17.5 terabytes"},{"index":5,"quote":"about 281 terabytes"}]},{"claim_text":"Joins are limited to 64 tables.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 7 states SQLite does not support joins containing more than 64 tables.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"SQLite does not support joins containing more than 64 tables."}]},{"claim_text":"There is no setting to change the join-table limit.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 states there is no mechanism to raise or lower the limit on the number of tables in a join.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"Hence, there is no mechanism to raise or lower the limit on the number of tables in a join."}]}]}
